need: A project worked on by several agent clients kept most of its lessons about its own tools in one client's private memory. The other clients and the owner never read them, so the same mistakes repeated under another client, and nobody reviewed the notes when the tools they described changed.
evidence: One project counted 160 notes in one client's memory, 112 of them naming files of the repository, while its two other clients held none. Moving them into the repository in nine batches left 22 notes, 6 naming a repository file. Most became a tool's own message, a check or a section of the page for that procedure. More than twenty described steps that had since been retired or were already enforced elsewhere, and two gave advice that had become wrong.
limits: Observed in one project with three agent clients, in one day of moving notes. This is guidance: the kit adds no check, because where a client keeps its memory differs by client; the source project guards one client with a hook of its own. Whether the moved lessons reduce repeated mistakes has not been measured. The source project does not install the kit, so this is a direct contribution rather than an installed-release export.
sanitization: Removed the project's client, tool, script and task names, host names and paths, and the contents of every note. No credentials, private account data, employer, client or third-party material is included.
